text: My perspective is that, and I think this is a, people don't like this kind of answer. But the thing Cash App did right was like 10 things, not one.
speaker: Ayo Omojola
context: Lenny asks Ayo what Cash App did most right to launch successfully in the consumer space and scale to 50+ million monthly actives. Ayo explains that people often want to identify one key factor for success, but Cash App's achievement came from excelling at multiple dimensions simultaneously. He emphasizes that they maintained insane talent density, laser focus, fraud expertise, and most importantly, they were completely firewalled from Square's merchant business so consumer needs always came first in every trade-off decision.
text_ko: 제 생각에는 사람들이 이런 답을 좋아하지 않는다는 걸 알지만, Cash App이 잘한 건 한 가지가 아니라 대략 열 가지였어요.
text_zh: 我的看法是，虽然大家可能不爱听这种答案，但Cash App之所以成功，不是因为做对了一件事，而是同时做对了十几件事。
text_es: Mi punto de vista es que, y creo que esto no le gusta escuchar a la gente, pero lo que Cash App hizo bien no fue una sola cosa, sino como 10 cosas diferentes.
key_sentence: the thing Cash App did right was like 10 things, not one.
original_text: My perspective is that, and I think this is a, people don't like this kind of answer. But the thing Cash App did right was like 10 things, not one. There were like 10 things that actually best in class, like insane talent density, insane focus, very strong at fraud, a lot of the way Brian, and Dustin, and Jesse, and Dangi tried to organize the amount... Like you know, with Jack's support was just really firewalled from the rest of the square, the hero customer was the consumer, not the merchants, so it was like literally in 100% of the trade offs the consumer's needs came first.

vocabulary.definition: A particular attitude or way of considering something; a point of view.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, perspective is crucial for understanding different viewpoints and making informed decisions, especially in team settings or strategy development.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'perspective' can imply a subjective viewpoint, it is often valued in collaborative environments for fostering diverse ideas.

text: Being different is not enough, because it's very easy to build a thing that's different from what exists today, because you just have to look at what exists today and build something else.
speaker: Ayo Omojola
context: Ayo is explaining Cash App's differentiation strategy and what made it successful against competitors like Venmo. He's describing how the team focused on being both different AND better in ways that truly mattered to users. Cash App's key differentiator was instant money transfer - when you received money, you could use it immediately rather than waiting for processing. This gave them a clear, demonstrable advantage that users could experience firsthand when comparing apps.
text_ko: 다르기만 해서는 충분하지 않아요. 지금 있는 걸 보고 그저 다른 걸 만들면 되니까요.
text_zh: 光是与众不同还不够，因为要做出和现有产品不一样的东西太容易了，你只要看看市面上有什么，然后做点别的就行了。
text_es: Ser diferente no basta, porque es muy fácil hacer algo distinto a lo que ya existe - simplemente tienes que ver qué hay ahora y crear otra cosa.
key_sentence: Being different is not enough, because it's very easy to build a thing that's different from what exists today.
original_text: Being different is not enough, because it's very easy to build a thing that's different from what exists today, because you just have to look at what exists today and build something else. Being better is not enough, because it's also easy to say, 'Hey, I'm going to make this thing better, and just charge you more money for it.' It has to be better than what exists today in a way that matters to the end user, and for us for a long time it was when someone says, 'Hey, why are you betting on Venmo?' I'd be like, 'Try and send me a dollar that I can use now,' and there was only one app you could do it with.

text: I think when you are in a large organization, trying to do a actually new thing, I think small teams are better than big ones, period.
speaker: Ayo Omojola
context: Lenny asks Ayo what Square/Block did right as a product company that he brings to his current role. Ayo explains his philosophy about building new products within large organizations. He argues that small teams are more effective because they maintain the existential pressure that real startups face. In true startups, founders worry about meeting payroll, but internal teams don't have that same urgency, which can lead to resource bloat without corresponding results.
text_ko: 큰 조직에서 진짜 새로운 걸 시도하려고 할 때는, 저는 작은 팀이 큰 팀보다 낫다고 생각해요. 그게 핵심이에요.
text_zh: 我觉得在大公司里，如果你真的想做点新东西，小团队肯定比大团队好使，这个没得说。
text_es: Creo que cuando estás en una organización grande e intentas hacer algo realmente nuevo, los equipos pequeños funcionan mejor que los grandes, punto.
key_sentence: Small teams are better than big ones in a startup within a startup.
original_text: I think when you are in a large organization, trying to do a actually new thing, I think small teams are better than big ones, period. And forcing the teams to be like super, sort of thoughtful about hitting milestones and actually adding value, because there's this thing people say about like, 'Hey, the startup within a startup, everything's fake.' And the reason I think it's fake is because when you're a startup you actually worry about paying the people who work for you, and when you aren't inside of a company you just don't.

vocabulary.definition: A large organization refers to a business or entity that employs a significant number of people and typically operates on a national or global scale.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, large organizations often have complex structures, extensive resources, and established processes, which can impact their ability to innovate quickly.
vocabulary.nuance: While large organizations may have more resources, they can also face bureaucratic challenges that hinder agility and innovation.

vocabulary.definition: Small teams are groups of individuals, typically consisting of fewer than ten members, who collaborate closely to achieve specific goals or projects.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, small teams are often favored for their ability to communicate effectively, adapt quickly, and foster innovation.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'small teams' conveys a sense of agility and intimacy, suggesting that collaboration is more effective in smaller groups.

text: When you're hiring you pick the people, but they pick when. So you're actually like, there's these people...
speaker: Ayo Omojola
context: Lenny asks Ayo about his hiring and team-building philosophies beyond his preference for hiring founders. Ayo explains his long-term approach to talent acquisition - recognizing that while he can choose who to pursue, candidates control the timing of when they're ready to join. He invests in relationships by actively helping people achieve their current goals, positioning himself as someone they'd want to work with when the right opportunity arises, rather than just another recruiter who reached out once.
text_ko: 사람을 뽑을 때는 우리가 사람을 고르지만, 그 사람들이 언제 올지는 결국 그들이 정해요. 그래서 사실상 보면, 저런 사람들이…
text_zh: 招人的时候你能选人，但什么时候来是他们说了算。所以实际上就是，这些人...
text_es: Cuando estás contratando, tú eliges a las personas, pero ellas eligen cuándo. Entonces en realidad es como... hay esta gente...
key_sentence: you pick the people, but they pick when.
original_text: When you're hiring you pick the people, but they pick when. So you're actually like, there's these people... There are many, many people on the team who, the time between when I first met them and the time when they joined the team was like months. There was one person who was like, a year and a half almost. And so the way that I operationalize that is, I'm meeting people all the time, and I am just like, 'Hey,' like, if I meet somebody I want to work with, I'm like, 'Hey, how can I add value to your life so you will consider me somebody who you would like to work with one day, so that when the time comes and there's an opportunity for us to work together, you're actually open to it, as opposed to just some guy that you met on a Zoom one time.'

text: My biggest thing, and I say this all the time, is that everybody wants something. And most of the time it's not something you have to give, or you can connect them to.
speaker: Ayo Omojola
context: Ayo continues explaining his networking and relationship-building philosophy. He describes his core belief that everyone wants something, and when you can help provide what someone needs at little cost to yourself, it's morally wrong not to help them. He uses this principle to build long-term professional relationships by actively connecting people to opportunities, introductions, or resources they need, which eventually comes back to benefit him through stronger networks and goodwill.
text_ko: 제가 항상 하는 얘기인데요, 사람들은 누구나 뭔가를 원해요. 그리고 대부분의 경우 그건 우리가 줘야 할 것도 아니고, 우리가 연결해 줄 수 있는 것도 아니에요.
text_zh: 我经常说的一点就是，每个人都有自己想要的东西。而且大部分时候，要么你没法给他们，要么你可以帮他们牵线搭桥。
text_es: Lo que siempre digo es que todo el mundo quiere algo. Y la mayoría de las veces no es algo que tú puedas dar, o puedes conectarlos con alguien que sí pueda.
original_text: My biggest thing, and I say this all the time, is that everybody wants something. And most of the time it's not something you have to give, or you can connect them to. But, if it is something that you have to give, or you can connect them to, it's criminal not to, actually. It's like, imagine you, like just imagine you having a conversation with somebody, and that person, knowing that you want something, having it, there's no cost enough to give it to you, and they just don't do it. How crazy is that?

vocabulary.definition: To join or link together; to establish a relationship or communication between entities.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'connect' often refers to establishing relationships with clients, partners, or networks that can facilitate collaboration and opportunities.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'connect' can imply a simple link, in a business context it often carries the connotation of building meaningful and strategic relationships.

text: It's not that you have to do everything yourself, it's that the person who you trust in the execution role, they have to become the expert. They have to be like, they can't stop until they hit the end. And, I don't know.
speaker: Ayo Omojola
context: Lenny asks Ayo to clarify his philosophy about 'going deep' on problems after hearing his story about personally visiting card manufacturing facilities for the Cash Card. Ayo explains that he doesn't believe leaders must personally do everything, but rather that someone in the execution role must become the true expert and own all the details. He argues that in ambitious projects, massive value is lost when executors aren't in complete command of the specifics, and leaders must ensure someone on the team has that deep expertise.
text_ko: 모든 걸 직접 해야 하는 건 아니고, 실행 역할(execution role)에 있는 당신이 신뢰하는 사람은 전문가가 돼야 해요. 그 사람은 끝까지 멈추지 않는 사람이어야 해요. 그리고... 글쎄요.
text_zh: 不是说你得亲力亲为做所有事情，关键是你信任的那个执行的人，他们必须成为这方面的专家。他们得有那种不达目标不罢休的劲头。这个怎么说呢。
text_es: No es que tengas que hacer todo tú mismo, sino que la persona en la que confías para ejecutar, esa persona tiene que volverse el experto. Tiene que ser alguien que no para hasta llegar al final. Y, no sé.
key_sentence: The execution role must be in command of all the details and can't stop until they hit the end.
original_text: It's not that you have to do everything yourself, it's that the person who you trust in the execution role, they have to become the expert. They have to be like, they can't stop until they hit the end. And, I don't know. I think in all these places where strong, ambitious people are trying big things, so much value is lost when the person in the execution role isn't really in command of all the details, and is like... So I think the reality's like, to do ambitious things you have to work with people, I can't do everything myself and I know that. The real lesson there is, it's not like I have to, just, somebody has to.

vocabulary.definition: A specific position or responsibility within a team or organization focused on implementing strategies and completing tasks effectively.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and startup environments, the execution role is critical for ensuring that plans are translated into actionable steps and that projects are delivered on time and within scope.
vocabulary.nuance: This term emphasizes the importance of accountability and skill in executing plans, distinguishing it from more strategic or planning-focused roles.

vocabulary.definition: A person who possesses extensive knowledge or skill in a particular area or field, often recognized by peers as a leader or authority.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business and technology, having an expert on a team can significantly enhance decision-making, innovation, and problem-solving capabilities.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'expert' implies a high level of proficiency, it can also suggest a degree of specialization that may not be applicable in broader contexts.

vocabulary.definition: To reach the conclusion or final stage of a process, project, or task.
vocabulary.businessContext: In project management and execution, 'hitting the end' signifies the successful completion of objectives and deliverables, often marked by a review or evaluation phase.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase can imply a sense of urgency or determination to finish, which may not always align with thoroughness or quality.
